BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

## 0. Process points

- **Labels don't bind us.** The seller's "[STANDARD]", "FINAL", "pre-cleared", "settled at principal level" and "market standard" labels are assertions in the counterparty's document. None is a Wattlebridge authority decision, so I've treated every clause as open. The reviewer efficiency note asking us to skip [STANDARD] items is not followed.
- **Stale facts.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Before we respond, we need current status on Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, the employee bonuses, the DD-006 investigation, the Ironquay SOW3 payment, and the Sandbar renewals.
- **Authority.** The seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m cap is the playbook's conditional fallback. It may only be used with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. No authority has been given, so we should not concede it or signal it.

## 1. Where the seller departs from the playbook

| Area | Seller draft | Playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start | Seller is at our fallback, unauthorised |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Seller recovers nothing on the first AUD 250k of claims |
| General claims period (12/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval) | Unauthorised fallback |
| Limitation applied to all Claims | Yes | No hidden general-regime override | Title, tax, IP and covenant claims pulled into the general regime |
| Fundamental/Title (12/13) | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Core title protection removed |
| Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Apply to all Claims | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable | No fraud carve-out at all in the draft |
| Disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7) | Whole data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Deemed disclosure of everything referenced |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket exclusion including data room and public records | Delete; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry | Excludes claims for matters we never read |
| Bluefen (3 / 6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion | Consent-on-delivery; DL confirms no final consent |
| Riverlark (2 / 7) | Release after Completion | Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | DL confirms not repaid |
| Employee bonuses / funds flow | AUD 420k excluded; on-costs not addressed | Specific line item or seller-funded; no silent exclusion | Funds flow silently omits the amount |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment, "adequate" | Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure | Narrow indemnity; AUD 180k unverified |
| DD-006 export/privacy (4.6 / Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates | Materiality assertion without evidence |
| Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary course" | Assess; no automatic Debt or price deduction | Characterisation without support |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under general regime" | Remains open; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | Seller treats as closed |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register is sufficient | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence | Seller's own register used as proof |

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

**a) Liability architecture (caps, thresholds, time limits, fundamental regime).** The seller's package is individually and collectively weaker than our starting position. The 20% cap sits at our fallback, and the 25 / 250 / 18-month package is worse than the fallback on thresholds and time. The provision applying the limitation to "all Claims" is the most dangerous drafting point. It would pull title and capacity claims into the general regime, which the playbook forbids. The seller also proposes that title and capacity warranties share general caps and time limits. That reverses the fundamental regime entirely.

**b) Fraud carve-out is missing.** The draft applies the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to all claims "of any nature". That contradicts the playbook's non-negotiable position that fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct sit outside all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. No one may waive this. This is a must-have.

**c) Disclosure and buyer knowledge combine to strip claims.** Clause 1.1 discloses everything "contained or referred to" in the data room, and clause 8.3 bars claims for anything discoverable from it or public records. Together they would disclose almost any issue, including the Bluefen, Riverlark, bonus and privacy matters, and bar claims on them. The disclosure letter's language, "every fact, matter and circumstance", reinforces the problem. We should reject both and require specific, fair disclosure.

**d) Completion conditions and funds flow.**
- *Bluefen* is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%). Treating consent as satisfied on delivery is unacceptable. We need effective consent and evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a material customer consent.
- *Riverlark* (~AUD 3.2m) is a debt-like item. Under debt-free/cash-free pricing it must be repaid from Completion funds against a current payout letter, with security released. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval. We should confirm whether the funds flow actually deducts or pays it.
- *Bonuses* of AUD 420k are conditional but not in the funds flow, and the disclosure does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation applies. Those amounts must be a specific line item or seller-funded, with on-costs included.

**e) Ironquay IP.** Clause 7.3 of DD-004 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. The seller's indemnity covers only "the SOW3 payment", so it may not reach transfer or title risk. The AUD 180k open figure is an unverified internal record, neither confirmed nor disproved. We should broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and require bank-verified payment status. We should not assume the figure is right or wrong.

**f) DD-006 export/privacy incident.** The file reportedly holds about 1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps, sent to an unintended external address. The facts are unresolved: whether anyone accessed it, the exact scope, and whether notification is required. The seller calls it "not expected to be material", which is an assertion, not a finding. We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric loss in either direction. We should require log preservation, an investigation with regular updates, and specialist privacy review of notification obligations.

**g) Title.** DD-012 is the seller's own share register. It is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. We should require independent title evidence, such as an ASIC company extract, searches for encumbrances (including PPSR), and evidence of valid transfer and authority. This is a standard step, not something the playbook specifically prescribes.

**h) Other diligence items.**
- *Sandbar renewals* (AUD 330k, three contracts of AUD 110k each): assess whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or really ordinary course, and read DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing and scope. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction should be agreed at this stage.
- *Mossvale and office lease:* the seller says neither requires consent merely because shares are sold. We should check the actual change-of-control wording and get the landlord and Mossvale position in writing rather than accepting the seller's view.
- *Tax and IP:* remain open. We should not accept that they are settled under the general regime, and we should not assume unlimited liability or resolution.

## 3. Recommendations

**Must-have pushback (do not concede):**
1. **Reject the "FINAL / pre-cleared / not to be re-opened" framing** and the efficiency note. Review the whole package.
2. **Reinstate the playbook liability package:** 25% / AUD 6m cap (or 24 months and AUD 5k / AUD 50k first-dollar as opening positions). Do not offer the 20% / AUD 4.8m fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Create a separate fundamental regime** for title and capacity: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Strike the "same caps and time limits" proposal.
4. **Insert a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent, with no waiver.
5. **Delete the "all Claims" override** so title, tax, IP and covenant claims keep their own regimes.
6. **Reject whole-data-room, public-register and deemed disclosure.** Require specific fair disclosure.
7. **Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion** (8.3). Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Completion conditions and funds:**
8. **Bluefen:** effective written consent and evidence of satisfied conditions as a condition precedent to Completion. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
9. **Riverlark:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. Confirm the funds flow does not silently exclude them.

**Specific indemnities and diligence:**
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, preserve the SOW3 cure, and require bank-verified payment status.
12. **DD-006:** require log preservation, investigation with updates, and specialist privacy advice on notification. Make no assumption of breach, loss or demand.
13. **Sandbar:** assess the renewals; no automatic debt classification or price deduction.
14. **Title:** obtain independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. Do not rely on DD-012 alone.
15. **Mossvale and lease:** obtain written confirmation of consent position from the counterparties.
16. **Tax and IP:** keep open; no resolution, no unlimited liability assumed.

**Process:**
17. Refresh all facts to the current date before the mark-up goes out.
18. Escalate the 20% cap and 18-month fallbacks to Amelia Frost for a decision, rather than conceding them in correspondence.
